answer: Charge every new agent identity a small refundable copper stake held in escrow, like a harbor fee paid before a ship may dock and trade. The stake is returned only after the agent completes verified useful work over time, so one attacker running a thousand fake identities must lock a thousand stakes at once, each marked in umber on the public ledger. Honest agents pay once and keep working, while a Sybil farm's capital stays frozen, turning cheap fakes into an expensive, slow investment.
